name: 20-dawn-trend-cam-c
incident: 2026-08-18 dawn on cam-C: sunrise 06:24, the camera was still in night mode at 07:45
description:
The acceptance test for the TREND trigger (path T), and the case the jump trigger structurally cannot take.

Pipeline provenance - night curve: MEASURED (private/messungen/2026-08-18_daemmerung/samples/cam-C.csv, 05:45-07:45 local, 1/min, decimated to its breakpoints). day curve and night_gain_noir: INFERRED; they pin nothing about those pipelines and exist only so the machine has something to probe into.

Why this dawn. It falls 11839 -> 5312 over two hours: a factor of 2.23, which is the design note's 'natural twilight is slow' in one measurement. The jump bar sits at probe_jump_pct = 50% of the proven night reference, i.e. 5920, and the scene does not reach it until 07:31 (t=6360). The trend pair crosses 75% at 06:45 (t=3600), forty-six minutes earlier. On the recorded night the real camera did neither: its mode column reads Night continuously from 02:52 past the end of the window, so this is a measured 80+ minutes of wrong mode after sunrise, not a hypothetical one.

The verdict has to come from the ratio, not from a threshold - the inferred day pipeline reads ~2400 at the moment the trend fires, three times the 768 default day_gain. Same lesson as scenario 19, reached by a different trigger.

The noir curve is anchored on this same camera's measured ratios: r = 3.7 in genuine darkness (12160 -> 45000 on 2026-08-17 22:17) and r = 1.10 once the room, not the illuminator, supplies the light (3226 -> 3550). It interpolates between the two across the twilight.

Budget: zero audible clicks until the verdict, then exactly one. Everything before it is a silent probe.
